repository: pytorch/pytorch title: Choose rounding mode when casting to dtype github_labels: module: cuda|triaged|module: type promotion|function request|oncall: pt2|module: inductor|module: floatx (formerly float8)|bot-triaged body_excerpt: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `tensor.to(dtype)` performs a round-nearest conversion. This makes sense in most cases, but there are situations where other rounding modes are useful. For example in MXFP8 (microscaled float8) on Blackwell GPUs, we need to convert the scales to their next power of 2 and convert them to a float8_e8m0fnu (i.e., a biased uint8). This could be done in one shot via `scales.to(torch.float8_e8m0fnu, round="up")`. Which then would allow PyTorch to match this exactly to the optimized PTX instruction `cvt.rp.satfinite.ue8m0x2.f32` (`.rp` means round-positive). ### Alternatives Several less-readable alternatives, which will also make it harder for PyTorch and Inductor to understand the intent and thus optimize the code. For example one could go through torch.log and torch.ceil, or through torch.frexp, or do the cast with round-nearest and the conditionally adjust the result. ### Additional context _No response_ cc @ptrblck @msaroufim @eqy @jerryzh168 @tinglvv @nWEIdia @nairbv @mruberry @voznesenskym @penguinwu @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @ipiszy @kadeng @muchulee8 @amjames @chauhang @aak...

repository: triton-lang/triton title: feat(examples): implement vllm in triton github_labels: body_excerpt: Vllm uses paged memory and has kernels that perform the generation part of the causal inference. The computation pattern of generation part - single Q for entire seq len of KV - is very different from computing the context part (which benefits from seq length parallelism over Q and hence flash attention). In this case, the bottleneck should be memory, as the KV values cannot be reused over the Q seq len, so it is an interesting question to ask how to tradeoff latency and parallelism with compute efficiency. In this case, batching similar seq length inference is very important. I also wonder if distributed shared memory and TMA optimizations would be beneficial here since it is so memory-bottlenecked. It would be interesting to implement this in triton and see whether triton can match or exceed the performance. repository: jax-ml/jax title: Should gradients of logsumexp([-inf, -inf]) be 0s instead NaNs? github_labels: bug|P2 (eventual) body_excerpt: Consider this snippet ```python import jax import jax.numpy as jnp def f(x): return jax.nn.logsumexp(jnp.stack([-jnp.inf, -jnp.inf + x])) jax.grad(f)(1.) ``` The computation inside `f` is essentially what happens inside the dynamic program of the CTC loss and similar losses that calculates a shortest distance over the log semiring. There, `-jnp.inf` is really "log(0)", and we can see that `(0 + 0 * exp(x))`'s gradient w.r.t. `x` should indeed be 0. Right now, the gradients are NaN instead because the gradients of `logsumexp([-inf, -inf])` are NaNs.
